home.title:
The decentralized infrastructure
for stablecoin ecosystems
home.description: A revolutionary stablecoin protocol enabling trigger redemptions and enhanced stability. Use and build apps that leverage EVM as a secure base layer.
home.whyTectonicDesc: More flexibility, more composability, more security. Major upgrades across the entire Tectonic ecosystem.
home.futurePaymentsDesc: Tectonic is a fully collateralized stablecoin protocol built for the EVM ecosystem. By combining reserve-backed stability, equity participation, and automatic trigger redemptions, it provides a secure foundation for next-generation payment infrastructure.
home.liveOnLeadingChainsDesc: Tectonic is deployed across multiple EVM-compatible chains. Choose a deployment to explore, mint, and earn.
home.stabilityPaymentsTitle: Built for Stability. Made for Payments.
home.stabilityPaymentsDesc: Tectonic uses trigger redemptions to maintain high reserve ratios without ever disabling minting. This keeps stablecoins available when payments matter.
home.howItWorksDesc: The protocol flow is straightforward: deposit a native asset, mint a stablecoin, use or redeem it, and rely on automatic safety mechanisms to keep the reserve healthy.

1.title: Deposit Native Asset
1.desc: Users deposit the blockchain's native asset into the protocol.

2.title: Mint StableCoin
2.desc: The protocol issues stablecoins backed by the reserve.

3.title: Use or Redeem
3.desc: Users can use the stablecoins for payments or redeem them back for the reserve asset.

4.title: Automatic Safety Protection
4.desc: If reserve levels become unsafe, the protocol can trigger redemptions to restore the reserve ratio and maintain the peg.

home.joinCommunityDesc: Be part of the next generation of stablecoin infrastructure. Connect with builders, researchers, and enthusiasts.

triggerRedemptions.title: Trigger Redemptions
triggerRedemptions.desc: Unique mechanism ensuring protocol stability through automatic redemptions at predetermined rates.

secureBaseLayer.title: Secure Base Layer
secureBaseLayer.desc: Built on EVM with battle-tested security. Leverage blockchain's immutable infrastructure.

evmCompatible.title: EVM Compatible
evmCompatible.desc: Deploy on any EVM-compatible chain. Maximum interoperability and reach.

defiIntegration.title: DeFi Integration
defiIntegration.desc: Seamlessly integrate with existing DeFi protocols. Composable by design.

footnotes.1: Decentralization: absence of a single controlling party over the protocol.
footnotes.2: Asset Backing: presence of assets that support the stablecoin's value.
footnotes.3: In contrast to popular misbeliefs, seigniorage-share based stablecoins are not backed by seigniorage shares.
footnotes.4: In contrast to popular misbeliefs, crypto-collateralized stablecoins are unbacked. The collateral is not a reserve. It is collateral for a loan that belongs to the borrower.
footnotes.5: Lending Independence: the stablecoin does not require an underlying loan or debt position to exist.
footnotes.6: A crypto-collateralized stablecoin is created only when a user opens a loan (CDP). Its existence directly depends on that debt position.
footnotes.7: Transparency: public visibility of reserves or positions.
footnotes.8: Knowing whether a fiat-backed stablecoin is sufficiently backed requires trusting the issuer or auditors.
footnotes.9: Redemption Rights: ability to exchange the stablecoin for underlying assets.
footnotes.10: Despite regulation requirements, fiat-backed stablecoin redemption at face value is usually limited to verified institutional partners. Retail users typically must rely on selling on open markets instead.
footnotes.11: A crypto-collateralized stablecoin is a loan note. Only the original borrower can redeem it directly for the locked collateral. Other holders can claim collateral only by bidding during a liquidation event. Otherwise, they must rely on selling on open markets.
footnotes.12: Leverage: ability to create a leveraged position using the model.
footnotes.13: Crypto-collateralized stablecoins support leveraged long positions only indirectly. The borrower mints stablecoins and sells them for more of the collateral asset.
footnotes.14: Crypto-backed stablecoins support leveraged long positions directly, through the minting of a separate coin that tokenizes the reserve surplus.
footnotes.15: Tectonic inherits the same direct leverage approach of crypto-backed stablecoins. But, thanks to its greater capital efficiency, it offers greater leverage.
footnotes.16: Minting: ability to mint new supply.
footnotes.17: Minting fiat-backed stablecoin for fiat at face value is usually limited to verified institutional partners. Retail users typically must rely on buying on open markets instead.
footnotes.18: Minting is only possible when the stablecoin's price is above the peg.
footnotes.19: Minting is disabled when the reserve ratio is below a threshold.
footnotes.20: Revenue Sources: where protocol income originates.
footnotes.21: Revenue Beneficiaries: who receives that income.
footnotes.22: Capital Efficiency: amount of stablecoin value created per unit of locked collateral.
footnotes.23: Fiat-backing stablecoins are very capital efficient because the reserve assets are presumably very stable and thus the issuing company can maintain a reserve ratio close to 100%.
footnotes.24: Seigniorage-share-based stablecoins are the most capital efficient of all because, being unbacked, they don't require capital at all.
footnotes.25: Crypto-collateralized stablecoins are the most capital inefficient because the collateral surplus must remain locked and idle.
footnotes.26: Crypto-backed stablecoins are more capital efficient than crypto-collateralized ones because their reserve surplus is tokenized and the reserve surplus tokens can be used freely and productively. Crypto-backed stablecoins are less capital efficient than fiat-backed stablecoins because their reserve assets are more volatile and thus a greater reserve ratio needs to be maintained in order to cushion against crashes in the reserve asset's price.
footnotes.27: Tectonic is more capital efficient than other crypto-backed stablecoins because its greater resilience against depegging allows it to maintain a lower reserve ratio.
footnotes.28: Depeg Resilience: ability of the model to prevent depegging or recover from depegging.
footnotes.29: Although depegging is unlikely because the reserve investments are supposed to be safe, these investments may still fail and cause the reserve ratio to drop below 100%. In such an event, recovery is unlikely.
footnotes.30: The Terra collapse shows that seigniorage-share-based stablecoins are unable to recover from depegging.
footnotes.31: The liquidation mechanism allows quick recovery of the collateral ratio if it becomes dangerously low. This indirectly protects the peg. Stablecoins of this kind have already successfully withstood several market crashes.
footnotes.32: Typical crypto-backed stablecoins maintain a large reserve ratio and are unlikely to depeg. Stablecoins of this kind have already successfully withstood several market crashes. However, if they depeg, recovery is difficult, to the lack of a liquidation-like mechanism. Recovery depends on recovery of the reserve asset or on the willingness of users to redeem stablecoins at discounted rates or to mint reserve surplus tokens at unfavorable prices.
footnotes.33: Tectonic triggers automatic redemptions for a random selection of users if the reserve ratio becomes dangerously low. This is a liquidation-like mechanism that directly protects the reserve ratio and the peg. However, unlike in liquidations, users receive exactly the amount of reserve assets that their stablecoins were worth, without any penalty.
